finalText:
# NIST SP 800-63B-4: password requirements for verifiers and CSPs

All three workers confirmed that the current revision is **NIST SP 800-63B-4**. They opened https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html, which is titled "NIST SP 800-63B-4, Digital Identity Guidelines: Authentication and Authenticator Management". The page is dated 26 Aug 2025 and says it "supersedes NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-63B". Every requirement below comes from section 3.1.1.2, "Password Verifiers", on that page.

| Topic | Keyword | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Minimum length, password as the only factor | SHALL | 15 characters |
| Maximum length | SHOULD | permit at least 64 characters |
| Composition rules | SHALL NOT | none |
| Periodic change | SHALL NOT | none |
| Password hints | SHALL NOT | none |
| Security questions / knowledge-based authentication | SHALL NOT | none |
| Blocklist check | SHALL | none |
| Password managers and autofill | SHALL (allow) | none |
| Salt length | SHALL | at least 32 bits |
| Approved SP 800-132 hashing scheme | SHOULD | none |

## Related points from the same section

- **Shorter passwords:** a password used only within multi-factor authentication MAY be shorter than 15 characters. It SHALL still be at least 8 characters.
- **Forced changes:** verifiers SHALL force a password change if there is evidence the authenticator has been compromised.
- **Hashing:** salting and hashing passwords with a suitable scheme is a SHALL. Using an *approved* scheme from SP 800-132 is only a SHOULD.

## Gaps

- The workers did not open the 2017 Revision 3, so the two revisions were not compared.
- The CSRC page https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/63/b/4/final returned a 404. Every finding therefore rests on the single pages.nist.gov source.
- The workers found no disagreement among the sources they opened.
